reason: I'll start with filtering so I can follow what leaves the blood before useful substances are recovered.
expectation: I expect small substances, including glucose and waste, to pass into the filter space while blood cells and large proteins stay in the blood.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would start the separate route to the bladder, but I want to follow filtration first.

effect: The filter lets useful glucose, water and salts through along with wastes, so the recovery tube is the next part to follow.
reaction: It was interesting that the filter doesn't just remove waste.
reason: The tube's picture shows useful substances returning to blood, directly continuing the filtering goal.
expectation: I expect glucose, some salts and much of the water to return to the blood, while waste stays in the tube.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would start the bladder route, but I want to finish following recovery first.

effect: Useful substances and much water return to the blood, leaving waste-containing fluid to collect in the bladder.
reaction: It makes sense why filtering alone wasn't enough.
reason: I'll add the ureters to start the route from the kidneys toward the bladder.
expectation: I expect the two tubes to connect to the kidney outlets, with the bladder still to be added.

alternatives.reason: The bladder also needs fitting, but the ureters connect the kidneys to it.

effect: The ureters now connect to the kidneys and point toward the bladder.
reaction: The tube route is clear so far.
reason: Adding the bladder is the only offered combination and completes the route for collecting urine.
expectation: I expect the ureters to connect to the bladder, giving urine a place to collect.

effect: The ureters now connect the kidneys to the bladder, completing the drainage route; the remaining fluid still needs to be collected.
reaction: Seeing the complete route makes the separate fittings clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should bring the remaining fluid into the completed drainage route.
expectation: I expect the waste-containing fluid to travel through the ureters and collect in the bladder as urine.

effect: The remaining fluid reached the bladder through the ureters, completing both goals.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the filtering and drainage routes come together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Filtering and then recovering useful substances was most worthwhile: it showed why the kidneys do more than just remove waste.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the bladder was fairly predictable after adding the ureters, though it completed a clear route.

surprise.text: I was surprised that useful glucose and water pass through the filter along with waste and have to be recovered.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless. The last combination was the only offered action, but its purpose was clear: collect the remaining fluid.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: following the filter and recovery process made a familiar organ's job more understandable, and I would be curious to see another system explained that way.
